New York Climate Hazards & Storm Durability

Selecting the correct shingle material and fastening schedule depends heavily on New York's prevailing weather patterns:

Climate & Storm Factor Regional Profile & Recommended Shingle Defense
Climate Overview Humid Continental: Severe Great Lakes lake-effect snow in upstate, coastal storms in Long Island/NYC.
Hail Exposure Risk Moderate — In moderate to extreme zones, UL 2218 Class 4 impact shingles are recommended.
Wind Velocity Risk High (Upstate gusts & coastal gales) — Requires ASTM D7158 Class H wind-rated shingles with enhanced 6-nail patterns.
Freeze-Thaw Cycling High to Extreme — Ice barrier self-adhering membranes required along eaves in freeze zones.
Licensing Authority No single state license; regulated by counties and municipalities (e.g. NYC DCA, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester).
Adopted Building Code New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code (2020/2021 IRC) & NYC Building Code.
Local Permitting Notes Local town/city building permits required; ice-and-water protection mandatory on all upstate sloped roofs.

Recommended Shingle Materials for New York Homes

Our network of independent contractors installs and replaces all seven major shingle roofing systems across New York:

Asphalt Shingle Installation

$380 – $580 per square

Asphalt shingles are North America's most popular residential roofing system, combining cost-effectiveness, proven Class A fire protection, and rapid installation.

Lifespan: 20 to 30 Years Impact: Class 3 to Class 4 (UL 2218)

Wood & Cedar Shingle Installation

$750 – $1,250 per square

Natural cedar shingles and hand-split shakes deliver authentic rustic charm, natural insulating R-value, and organic architectural elegance.

Lifespan: 30 to 45 Years (with maintenance) Impact: Class 3 (natural resistance)

Metal Shingle Installation

$850 – $1,400 per square

Engineered stone-coated steel and stamped aluminum shingles combine the traditional aesthetic of slate, tile, or shake with the indestructible strength of metal.

Lifespan: 50 to 70 Years Impact: Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 rating)

Rubber Shingle Installation

$800 – $1,350 per square

Engineered from up to 95% recycled automotive tires and virgin polymers, recycled rubber shingles offer near-indestructible impact resistance, eco-sustainability, and authentic slate-shake styling.

Lifespan: 50+ Years Impact: Class 4 (Superior hail deflection)

Composite Shingle Installation

$950 – $1,600 per square

Engineered from virgin resins and mineral reinforcements, composite synthetic slate and shake shingles deliver luxury aesthetics, Class 4 impact resistance, and a 50-year lifespan without structural reinforcement.

Lifespan: 50+ Years Impact: Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 certification)

Slate Shingle Installation

$1,500 – $3,000 per square

Quarried natural stone slate represents the pinnacle of luxury roofing, offering non-combustible fire protection and unmatched structural durability lasting 75 to over 100 years.

Lifespan: 75 to 100+ Years Impact: Class 3 to 4 (dependent on stone thickness)

Solar Shingle Installation

$2,100 – $3,800 per square (before tax credits)

Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) seamlessly integrate clean solar energy generation directly into sleek, low-profile shingle tiles without bulky rack-mounted solar panels.

Lifespan: 25 to 30 Years (power output warranty) Impact: Class 3 to 4 (Tempered solar glass)

New York Roofing Questions

Do roofing contractors in New York need to be licensed?

No single state license; regulated by counties and municipalities (e.g. NYC DCA, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester). All independent contractors in the American Shingle Co. network must verify compliance with applicable state and local jurisdiction licensing and insurance requirements.

Are building permits required for roof replacement in New York?

Local town/city building permits required; ice-and-water protection mandatory on all upstate sloped roofs. In virtually all incorporated areas, a building permit must be obtained prior to initiating a complete roof tear-off and replacement.

What is the best shingle material for homes in New York?

For most New York homeowners, architectural asphalt shingles provide the best balance of value, Class A fire protection, and 130 mph wind defense. In areas with moderate hail exposure, Class 4 impact-resistant stone-coated metal or recycled rubber shingles provide maximum longevity.
